Basal Cell Skin Cancer
Basal cell skin cancer, also known as basal cell carcinoma (BCC), is the most common type of skin cancer.

Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)
Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is another name for basal cell skin cancer.

Sun
Sun is the source of ultraviolet (UV) radiation that contributes to the development of basal cell skin cancer.

Basal Cells
Basal cells are cells in the lower epidermis that constantly divide and can become abnormal in basal cell skin cancer.

Surgery
Surgery is the primary treatment method involving removal of the cancerous tissue.

UV Radiation
UV radiation is a form of electromagnetic radiation emitted by the sun and tanning beds that can damage DNA.

Tanning Beds
Tanning beds are devices that emit UV radiation and are a risk factor for basal cell skin cancer.

United States
United States is the country where approximately 3 million cases of basal cell skin cancer are diagnosed each year.

DNA
DNA contains the genetic information that regulates cell growth and can be damaged by UV radiation.

NCCN Guidelines for Patients
NCCN Guidelines for Patients provide information and recommendations for skin cancer diagnosis and treatment.

Metastasis
Metastasis refers to the spread of cancer cells to distant tissues; basal cell skin cancer rarely metastasizes.

Skin Lesions
Skin lesions are abnormalities on the skin, including basal cell lesions, commonly found in basal cell skin cancer.
